requirement: Evaluate a classifier on repeated measurements per patient using grouped cross-validation, so the score reflects generalization to unseen patients, with validation of group counts and alignment.
skeleton: A frozen CVResult dataclass and grouped_cv_score validating group alignment and count, then calling cross_val_score with GroupKFold and returning scores, mean and sample std.
caption: Cross-validating with scikit-learn when several rows belong to the same patient, so no patient appears in both training and test folds. CVResult is a frozen dataclass of a scores tuple, mean and std. grouped_cv_score(model, x, y, groups, *, n_splits=5) raises ValueError saying groups must align with y when their lengths differ, and raises ValueError saying it needs at least n_splits groups when there are fewer distinct groups. It converts groups with numpy and runs cross_val_score with that array, cv set to GroupKFold with n_splits and accuracy scoring, and returns the scores as floats with their mean and sample standard deviation using ddof 1. The fixture asserts that a 1-nearest-neighbour model scoring near perfect with plain five-fold drops below 0.8 when grouped, that scores match GroupKFold directly with the sample std, that exactly n_splits groups works, that four groups raises ValueError, that misaligned groups raise ValueError, and that the model is not fitted in place.

plan.intent: Estimate accuracy on new patients honestly
constraints: Groups whose length differs from y raise ValueError
Fewer distinct groups than n_splits raise ValueError
Folds come from GroupKFold using the real groups
The std is the sample standard deviation with ddof 1

rationale.teaches: Pass groups through cross_val_score with GroupKFold so correlated rows never straddle folds, and validate the grouping before relying on it.
rationale.why: Row-level folds let a model memorize each patient and report near-perfect scores that collapse on new patients, and population std understates fold variance.

ops.docstring: Cross-validate with GroupKFold so no group spans train and test folds.

ops.source:
def grouped_cv_score(
    model: BaseEstimator,
    x: ArrayLike,
    y: ArrayLike,
    groups: ArrayLike,
    *,
    n_splits: int = 5,
) -> CVResult:
    """Score ``model`` by accuracy with GroupKFold over ``groups``."""
    group_arr = np.asarray(groups)
    if group_arr.shape[0] != np.asarray(y).shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("groups must align with y")
    n_groups = np.unique(group_arr).size
    if n_groups < n_splits:
        raise ValueError(f"need at least {n_splits} groups, got {n_groups}")
    scores = cross_val_score(
        model,
        x,
        y,
        groups=group_arr,
        cv=GroupKFold(n_splits=n_splits),
        scoring="accuracy",
    )
    return CVResult(
        scores=tuple(float(s) for s in scores),
        mean=float(np.mean(scores)),
        std=float(np.std(scores, ddof=1)),
    )

candidates.why_wrong: GroupKFold receives no groups and raises instead of producing scores.
Every row is its own group so a patient's rows leak across folds.
Exactly n_splits distinct groups is rejected though GroupKFold supports it.
The population standard deviation is reported instead of the sample one.
Misaligned groups surface as a generic scikit-learn length error instead.
